outcome: Chen, Ghomi and Wang posted a preprint (10 Sep 2026, extended 17 Sep 2026) claiming to prove the Cartan-Hadamard conjecture in dimensions 3 through 9, extending the previously established range of dimensions 2-4; the claim is a preprint with no expert digestion yet.

summary: The Cartan-Hadamard conjecture (sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for Cartan-Hadamard manifolds) was known, at the frozen revision's date, for dimensions 2 (Weil 1926; Beckenbach-Rado 1933), 3 (Kleiner 1992) and 4 (Croke 1984); Ghomi and Spruck's widely-publicized 2019 claim of a full unconditional resolution was found to have a gap in early 2020, and their eventual published (2022, J. Geom. Anal.) result reduces the general conjecture to a total-curvature inequality rather than proving it outright — so the conjecture remained genuinely open in dimension >= 5 through the frozen date. In September 2026, Shibing Chen, Mohammad Ghomi and Peng Wang posted arXiv:2609.11005 (10 Sep 2026), proving the conjecture in dimension 5 via a sharp inequality for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces (in the spirit of Banchoff-Pohl) plus Jacobi-field estimates along geodesic chords, completed by a Kleiner-style isoperimetric-profile argument. A companion/extended paper by the same three authors, arXiv:2609.20517 (17 Sep 2026), extends the same method to give a unified proof covering all of dimensions 3-9 (also reproving dimension 3). One secondary source noted the dimension-5 argument leans on a regularity lemma (Ghomi-Spruck, Lemma 7.2) established only up to dimension 7, which is a detail worth flagging for anyone assessing the full 3-9 claim, but does not change the classification here. Both papers are very recent (5 and 12 days old at the time of this research) preprints with no journal acceptance, no Tao/Quanta/Terry Tao-blog digestion, and no independent expert verification found — hence `claimed` rather than `resolved`. The dimension-5 paper's acknowledgements disclose that 'The AI tools Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI) were used in the preparation of this manuscript,' with authors stating they reviewed all AI-assisted content and take full responsibility; no detail is given on what the AI tools actually did, and nothing suggests they produced any mathematical content (a proof step, construction, or bound) rather than writing/editing assistance. Per the rules, a bare disclosure of this kind without the authors attributing any specific mathematical contribution to the AI is `ai_role: none`. Two further preprints found by triage are related-problem or partial results, not the (candidate) full resolution: arXiv:2609.14505 (Wheeler, 13 Sep 2026) proves the isoperimetric inequality only under an added curvature-pinching hypothesis relative to a reference radius of curvature — a restricted/conditional variant, not the stated conjecture; arXiv:2609.17093 (Agnoletto, Da Silva, Nardulli, Resende; 15 Sep 2026, rev. 21 Sep 2026) proves only the small-volume regime under an added lower Ricci bound, reducing the remainder to a rigidity question — also a restricted case with an extra hypothesis. Neither reports AI involvement.
competing_reading: One could argue the dimension 3-9 result should be treated as `partial` rather than `claimed`, on the reasoning that dimensions 3 and 4 were already resolved before 2024 and only 5-9 is new territory; I chose `claimed` because the paper's claimed scope (a unified proof for 3<=n<=9) is presented as, and would constitute if correct, a resolution of a large new swath of the conjecture including previously-unproven dimensions 5-9, which is closer to a leap in coverage than a single new case, and no expert has yet reviewed it to promote it to `resolved`. A different reading of the AI disclosure is also possible: an editor might argue that any acknowledged use of an AI system, however vague, should be flagged as `assisted` out of caution; I did not do this because the rule explicitly requires the authors' own account of the AI producing part of the mathematics in the result, and this disclosure states only 'preparation of this manuscript' with no claim that Claude or ChatGPT produced any proof step.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (a referee report, journal acceptance, or a public write-up by another differential geometer such as on Terry Tao's blog or in a survey) confirming the dimension 3-9 argument is correct would move this to `resolved`; alternatively, a reported gap (as happened to Ghomi-Spruck in 2020) would keep it at `claimed`/`progress` or revert it. Clarification from the authors on exactly what Claude and ChatGPT were used for would settle whether `ai_role` should remain `none` or be reconsidered.

corrections.why: SCOPE: `claimed` counted this among resolutions, but Chen-Ghomi-Wang prove the conjecture in dimensions 3 to 9 (new in 5 to 9); it remains open in every dimension from 10 up. A range of dimensions is a case, `partial` under 6.1, which the record's own competing_reading raises. The research rules fold 'how much was settled' and 'has an expert checked it' into one field, and the agent read an unreviewed case as `claimed`; that is the pattern this batch of corrections fixes. `partial` does not record review status, so the absence of expert digestion, and the flagged regularity lemma proved only up to dimension 7, stay in `summary`.
